text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi criticises members of parliament who berate the country's leadership when they are abroad.
- Employees of the Kenya Railways Corporation strike, demanding March salaries.
- Three men are charged in a Nairobi court with trying to defraud the treasury of 159 million shillings.
- President Moi warns inflation is likely to go up while economic growth is likely to decline because of famine in Kenya.
- A policeman in the Rift Valley district of Trans Nzoia goes beserk, deserting his station and shooting dead his uncle.
- The government maintains the ban on game hunting will remain.
- Oppposition leaders declare war against the government for what they say is its refusal to come up with policies against famine, insecurity and social ills.
- Angry villagers from Makueni in eastern Kenya set ablaze a suspected member of a notorious gang.
- A bishop receives a suspended sentence for stealing money donated to his church for construction of a children's home. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
